_description: Plan 32 — the residual spectra: every residual series the model produces against an external record (ΔT: Espenak & Meeus 2006, Stephenson–Morrison–Hohenkerk 2016; LR04 per regime; the paleo anchors; the certified Sun and its cardinal instants against JPL Horizons; the lunar canon; the Earth's e, ε, ϖ against La2004), each through ONE harness (a generalised weighted Lomb–Scargle with AR(1) and white surrogate floors on the maximum over the grid, the edge/interior and two-halves splits), with the probes that read the lines (the named-argument table, the cardinal tier split and crossing interpolation, the lunar node-distance regression) and the decision's counts. GENERATED by tools/explore/residual-spectra/write-sweep.mjs --write; doc 112 and the registry's residualSweep* keys render from it.

closedByTheFollowUp.physics: the cos M′ term of the shipped instant's residual (the span mean of a term growing into the past: −0.5 / −2.0 / −5.7 min per millennium before 1000 in probes.lunarThirdInstrument; the sin M′ part of the opposition instant's 5-min pair was the definition offset's own form and left with the instant) — the model's perigee and node ride the deep eccentricity channel (the physical exponents s_ϖ, s_Ω on the model's own e(t)), Meeus-exact in T² by construction; their T³ is the channel's own ë, about a seventh of the secular-theory ë that ELP's polynomials embody — L′ carries that convention through lpSecularCompletion, ϖ and Ω do not (doc 66's "predicted-ë-vs-secular-ë" drift, here measured): the model's M′ runs ahead of the polynomial's by the complement, 0 in the fit window, 0.2° at −500, 0.54° at −1500, 1.66° at −3000
closedByTheFollowUp.closedBy: apsidalNodalSecularCompletion (moon/arguments.cjs): L′'s secular-ë carrier scaled to ϖ and Ω — the model's M′ within 0.04° of the polynomial over ±3,000 yr

decision.rule: a survivor with no external physics in ≥ 2 independent series reopens the theory; none → the framework stands and the next input is a cited ocean-dissipation history (plan 32 §0); a line standing WITH named physics in one series is an input, listed above
